findings.expected: Part (a) direct set includes 8227:2020:M1:T7:O02:D01 'Add and subtract vectors' (registry text; syllabus bullet 'perform addition and subtraction of vectors'), because criterion a:B1 credits the subtracted vector (p-s, rp-1, p+1) exactly as the official 2025 Q3(a) B1 credits pOA-OB.
findings.actual: Recipe lists O02:D03 'Interpret geometric vector relation' instead of D01, and the work order withholds the 2025 P1 Q3(a) same-type label because the source 'additionally includes M1:T7:O02:D01 (addition)'. D01 is add AND subtract; perpendicularity is already O05:D02, so D03 has no separate criterion.
findings.evidence: Native 2025 8227-1 p4 asks pOA - OB; report 2025 p347 B1 = components of pOA - OB. demand-registry D01 learner_action 'Add and subtract vectors'.
findings.repair: Replace D03 with D01 in part (a) (or justify D03 with its own criterion). Counts stay 38/25 but coverage-plan rows for D01/D03 change. Then re-judge the (a) same-type label on the equal demand sets; do not retag the accepted item.

findings.expected: If the pilot claims to combine 'modelling' demands, the syllabus modelling ability (8227:2020:ABILITY:08:MODEL, construct a model from geometric/contextual constraints) is exercised, or its absence is stated; every supplementary record carries a pilot disposition.
findings.actual: No pilot part carries ABILITY:08. Log-linear 'model' recovers parameters of a supplied model form. ABILITY:08 is directly tagged on 10 exam parts / 26 marks, Paper 1 in all five years (mostly show-that). The 8 non_specific_demands in coverage-plan have only id/scope, no pilot_disposition, so the 138-row accounting cannot show this omission.
findings.evidence: question-analysis: ABILITY:08:MODEL on 2021 P1 Q7a, 2022 P1 Q8a/Q12a, 2023 P1 Q6a/Q13a, 2024 P1 Q7a/Q11a/Q11b, 2025 P1 Q9a/Q10a. Native 2025 P1 p12 Q9(a) 'Express h ... show that A = ...' [4].
findings.repair: Either reword PLAN line 15 (e.g. 'transformed-model parameter recovery') and give ABILITY:08 and the 7 PRIOR records explicit later-scope dispositions, or add a branch that constructs a model from a given diagram (it could reuse the stationary two-extrema logic).

findings.expected: A framework pilot meant to prove 'contract/marking/visual/branch boundaries' either covers the show-that (answer-given) marking contract or explicitly records it as an untested contract feature.
findings.actual: 0 of 28 pilot parts are proof/show-that, against 44 of 250 exam parts and 131 of 750 marks (17.5%), every year. That contract (all credit on working; answer-only earns nothing; a given result can be used in later parts) is listed in recipe-contract.md:74 but is untested by the pilot. The 55 later groups all carry one templated reason, 'Not needed to prove the selected pilot contracts', which is exactly what is in doubt here. Given geometric diagrams (28 exam parts) are also absent.
findings.evidence: question-analysis response_format counts; pilot-design response_format counts {numeric 15, symbolic 8, explanation 4, sketch 1}.
findings.repair: Owner chooses: add one show-that branch (e.g. a constrained-optimisation 'show that A=...' then optimise, or a trig identity show-that reused in a bounded equation), or add a gap row (D8227-G0x) stating that show-that marking and given geometric diagrams stay untested until a later batch.

findings.expected: Each of the 28 slots has its own criterion-linked Bloom rationale (PLAN.md:32: 'All 28 ... criterion-linked proposals').
findings.actual: 14 of 28 slots reuse a recipe-level rationale. The gradient-only branch's single part cites the normal branch's N1/N2. The two-extrema parts cite 'P/I/C' criteria, which include the inflexion branch's I criteria. All six motion Apply slots share 'V/S/E/R ... signed-definite-integral'; interior-reversal:rest (1 mark, v=k(t-r)=0 so t=r) is labelled Apply 3 by text that describes integration. Levels and branch maxima are still computed correctly.
findings.evidence: Grouping register parts by identical rationale gives groups of 2 (vector), 3 (implicit), 3 (stationary) and 6 (motion).
findings.repair: Write a per-part rationale that cites only that part's criterion IDs, and re-judge interior-reversal:rest (Understand 2 is arguable; the branch maximum stays 4).

findings.locator: work-orders/WB8227-implicit-normal.md:33; planning/pilot-design.json implicit gradient part prerequisite_demand_ids=[]
findings.expected: Prerequisite links stated in the work order are recorded in the JSON part specs.

findings.repair: Add the prerequisite link to the JSON, or drop the sentence from the work order.

findings.locator: PLAN.md:89; planning/coverage-plan.json accepted_selection_dispositions (55 x templated reason)
findings.expected: The owner can see exam weight when choosing scope.
findings.actual: The heaviest examined groups are later scope with only the templated reason: function-analysis (20 parts, 39 share-marks, every year), numerical-method-chain (16 parts, every year), constrained-optimisation (10 parts, 4 of 5 P1 papers), quadratic-substitution, binomial, product-quotient, trig-integration. The only group present in all 10 papers (bounded-trig) enters the pilot only through the R-form route. 11 of the top-15 demands are pilot facets, but several only as narrow facets (e.g. M2:T3:O02:D05 only via R-form; 13 of its 17 exam parts use other identities). PLAN.md:89 does list these areas as retained, so nothing is hidden.
findings.evidence: exam_weight block in this file; SCRATCH/coverage/demand_freq.json, objective_freq.json
findings.repair: Add an exam-weight column (parts, marks, papers) to coverage-plan.md so Vitalis's scope choice is informed. No change of selection is required by this review.

findings.actual: It includes the vector branch, whose givens are text-only (work order line 48: 'No input figure is necessary'). Visual demands in the pilot are modulus (given graph), log graph-intercept (given graph, not in this deck) and trapezium (c) (learner sketch).

findings.expected: Pilot/later group status reflects which decisions the pilot exercises.
findings.actual: The 12/55 split follows declared recipe parentage, not decision overlap. Several later groups have their decision exercised: tangent-normal (forward normal at a point) by implicit normal:normal; definite-integral and standard-antiderivatives by the motion parts. This undercounts and is not an inflated claim.
findings.evidence: demand overlap between later-group demand lists and pilot parts (e.g. tangent-normal 3/6 demands, product-quotient 8/14).
findings.repair: None required. Optionally add a 'decision partly exercised by' cross-reference.
